name: Ankylosing Spondylitis / Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis
definition: Chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease predominantly affecting the sacroiliac joints and axial skeleton, with possible enthesitis, peripheral arthritis and extra-articular disease.

typical: Chronic back pain often beginning before age 45
Morning stiffness and improvement with exercise
Night pain or alternating buttock pain
Possible uveitis, psoriasis or inflammatory bowel disease

redFlags.item: Acute painful red photophobic eye suggesting uveitis
Neurological symptoms after minor trauma in an ankylosed spine
Cauda equina or severe cardiopulmonary complication

investigations.principle: Diagnosis combines clinical pattern, imaging and laboratory context.
investigations.MRI: SI-joint MRI can demonstrate active sacroiliitis in appropriate diagnostic pathways.
investigations.radiographs: Pelvic/SI radiographs identify structural sacroiliitis in radiographic disease.

green: Cardiovascular, bone-health and smoking risk management
amber: NSAIDs and biologic/targeted therapies require individualized medical assessment and monitoring.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Inflammatory axial disease should not be reduced to one Ayurvedic label; Ama/Vata and inflammatory features may be recorded as a parallel assessment.

patientEducation.summary: Chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease predominantly affecting the sacroiliac joints and axial skeleton, with possible enthesitis, peripheral arthritis and extra-articular disease.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
